title: Fung-AI prioritizes peptides with measured antifungal activity
summary: Fung-AI combines a generative adversarial network with learned antifungal and hemolysis classifiers to select peptides for testing. The study first tested five peptides from separate clusters; activity of peptide 40 prompted testing of eight more members from cluster 17. Five of the nine tested cluster-17 peptides inhibited Fusarium graminearum, a post-selection cluster-specific outcome—not a general 5/13 model hit rate. Four peptides showed activity against Candida albicans, while none inhibited C. auris up to 500 μg/mL. The paper’s HepG2 cytotoxicity statements are internally inconsistent for peptide 48 and peptide 65, and peptide 12 and 40 have reported cytotoxicity; these assays establish neither human safety nor clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Fung-AI GAN; learned antifungal and hemolysis classifiers
organization: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory; Johns Hopkins University

evidence.tested: Primary article reports staged testing, fungal MICs and cell-line cytotoxicity; adaptive denominator and conflicting LC50 statements were reconciled in the continuation audit.
evidence.unknown: Sequence-level prior art and independent replication not assessed; HepG2 assays do not establish human safety.
evidence.ai_role: GAN generates candidates; antifungal and hemolysis classifiers narrow the candidate set before synthesis and fungal assays.

source_review.scope: Primary PLOS article and indexed PMC full text checked; follow-up audit read full article and resolves staged denominator and LC50 inconsistency, not by remeasurement.
